title: Early size fits give no clear later wait-time gain for the Crab pulsar and PSR J1740-3015
abstract: We test whether a large pulsar spin jump predicts a long wait to the next event. We fit a line with a nonnegative slope and intercept to the first two thirds of usable catalog pairs. Later tests use nine Crab intervals and 13 PSR J1740-3015 intervals. The Crab fit assigns zero weight to size. The J1740-3015 fit reduces mean squared error by 11.2 percent, but independent early and later block resampling gives a range from -25.3 to 25.2 percent at block length two. A comparison on 15 later RXTE intervals of PSR J0537-6910 gives an 88.2 percent reduction. This known relation survives the same test. Alternate splits and fit rules do not establish a radio-source forecast gain. These are retrospective tests of selected catalog events, not independent timing measurements or tests of all stress models. Unknown missed events, changes in observing coverage and small test sets limit the result. Code, selected source rows, raw input hashes, figures and offline steps are included.

display.caption: Early and later size-to-wait pairs and frozen forecasts. The RXTE comparison retains the known size relation. The two radio sources give no clear later gain under the stated tests.

citations.reason: Prior size and wait tests in prolific pulsars; the strong J0537 relation is known.
Prior serial dependence and state-dependent trigger models.
Crab cluster analysis uses merged events and preceding waits. Our test uses individual events and following waits.
Shared input inventory and prior catalog-version audit. We add chronological forecast tests and reuse no analysis code.
Earlier RXTE-to-NICER validation of the known relation. Our comparison uses only RXTE events.
